What is on each chart

Every level appears on every timeframe, at the same thickness. A weekly band is 90 points on the weekly chart and 90 points on the 15-minute one — a level is a price band, so it cannot change size depending on what you are looking at.

The lower two panels show a wide window on purpose. Zoom a 15-minute chart to one week and gold only moves about 350 points, so a 90-point weekly band fills a quarter of the screen. That is not the band being wrong; it is what 90 points looks like when the whole view is 350. Your own chart does the same.

Two things worth checking

The prices are mine, read off your screenshot. Two screenshots agreed to about 10 points, so they are close — but they are my pixels, not your numbers. They are in config/levels/XAUUSD.toml and easy to correct.

The candles are cTrader, your chart is Pyth. Two feeds for the same metal. They will not agree to the cent, so a band drawn at 4000 on Pyth sits slightly off on this data. At 90 points wide it does not matter yet. It will matter when the broker is a third feed again.

Every level runs forward only

Each one carries the day it was drawn. Before that day it does not exist — not drawn, not checked, not tradeable.

A level drawn today knows what price did last year. Applying it backwards would make a backtest look better than anything you could have traded, which is the one mistake this whole design is built to prevent. Drawing them forward only costs nothing and keeps the numbers honest.
